title: Large Spanish EEG
description: A large EEG dataset of 60 sessions from 56 healthy Spanish-speaking participants, recorded with 64 channels during perception and silent production of 30 everyday Spanish sentences. It was collected to support subject-independent decoding of perceived sentences with deep neural networks, with the aim of enabling speech neuroprostheses that need no patient-specific training data.
methods_description: 64-channel EEG was recorded while participants listened to spoken sentences and then silently repeated them without motor action. Each trial had four segments: rest (5 s), perception (4 s before S18, 5 s from S19), preparation (1 s) and silent speech production (5 s). Sentences were repeated 7 times (before S19) or 6 times (from S19), and trial order was randomized within each block of 30 stimuli.
